x: Alfred Nobel (not 'Noble') invented dynamite in 1867; cosmic rays were discovered by Victor Hess.

s: RDX was invented by
x: RDX, the abbreviation of Research Department Explosive, is also called cyclonite. This powerful explosive was discovered by George Friedrich Henning of Germany and patented in 1898 but not used until World War II, when most of the warring powers introduced it.

s: Alfred Nobel invented –
x: Swedish scientist Alfred Nobel invented dynamite. The famous Nobel Foundation was established on the basis of his will in 1900.

s: In which of the following subject, Nobel Prize is not given
x: Nobel Prizes are given in Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Peace, with Economics added in 1968. Mathematics is not among them (it has the Fields Medal and Abel Prize instead).

s: Who established Nobel Prize in Economics?
x: Economics was not in Nobel's will; it was added in 1968 and first awarded in 1969. It was not established by Alfred Nobel, so the option naming the Central Bank of Sweden is the one that fits.

s: .................. was given first Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of X-ray?
x: Röntgen received the first Physics Nobel in 1901, for the discovery of X-rays.

s: The Nobel Prize was instituted by which country?
x: Alfred Nobel was Swedish and his will (1895) set up the prizes, so the Nobel Prize was instituted in Sweden.

s: In which year were the first Nobel Prizes awarded?
x: The first prizes were awarded in 1901; 1895 is the year of Alfred Nobel's will.

s: In which year was the Nobel Prize in Economics added?
x: Economics was added in 1968 and first awarded in 1969; it was not among the original five prizes of Nobel's will.

s: Which statement about Nobel laureate status is correct?
o: It can be revoked by the Nobel Committee after the award ceremony.
It automatically passes to the laureate's institution after death.
It may be transferred permanently to another person along with the medal.
It cannot be transferred, shared or revoked; only the physical medal can change hands.
x: Nobel laureate status cannot be transferred, shared or revoked. Only the physical medal can change hands.

s: In which year did Alfred Nobel invent dynamite?
x: Nobel invented dynamite in 1867; his will was made in 1895 and the first prizes given in 1901.

s: In which year was the Nobel Foundation established?
x: The Nobel Foundation was set up in 1900, after the 1895 will; the first prizes followed in 1901.

s: Which of the following was NOT one of the original five Nobel Prizes?
x: Economics was added in 1968 and is not in Nobel's will; the original five were Physics, Chemistry, Medicine, Literature and Peace.

s: Who invented RDX (cyclonite), patented in 1898?
x: RDX (cyclonite) was patented in 1898 by Georg Friedrich Henning of Germany, not by Alfred Nobel.

s: In which year was the Nobel Prize in Economics first awarded?
x: The Economics prize was added in 1968 and first given in 1969; it is not in Nobel's will.

s: Sir C.V. Raman received Nobel Prize for physics in the year :

Who of the following scientists proved that the stars with mass less than 1.44 times the mass of the sun end up as White Dwarfs when they die?
x: S. Chandrasekhar proved that the stars with mass less than 1.44 times the mass of the sun ends up as white dwarfs when they die. He showed that the mass of a white dwarf could not exceed 1.44 times that of the sun.

s: The principle of ‘Black hole’ was enunciated by :
x: Indian American astrophysicist Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar was best known for rendering the theory of 'Chandrasekhar Limit'. For this, he used Albert Einstein's special theory of relativity and the principle of quantum physics. Chandrasekhar showed that it is impossible for a white dwarf star to be stable if its mass is greater than 1.44 times that of the sun. If such a star does not completely exhaust its thermonuclear fuel, then this limiting mass may be slightly larger. A star that ends its nuclear-burning lifetime with a mass greater than the Chandrasekhar limit must be either a Neutron star or a black hole. For this contribution in astrophysics he was awarded the 1983 Nobel Prize in Physics with William A. Fowler.

Consider the following phenomena :

2. The Universe is constantly expanding.
3. Matter warps its surrounding space-time.
Which of the above is/are the prediction/predictions of Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity, often discussed in media?
x: When light travels near a huge celestial body like neutron star or black hole it bends towards the celestial body. Hence, statement 1 is correct. As per the prediction of Albert Einstein, the astronomers have found that the universe is expanding continuously and a heavenly body with huge mass tends to bend (warp) the space-time.
